paper.title: Second Chance: A Two-Bit Cache Eviction Policy for Bursty Web Traffic

abstract.anchor: Web caches evict objects when they run out of space

fifo.abstract.en: First-in first-out (FIFO) eviction is cheap but evicts popular objects that happened to arrive early.

sc.rule.en: Each object carries a reference bit. A hit sets the bit. When the cache is full, the eviction hand moves over the objects in arrival order. An object whose bit is set gets a second chance: the hand clears the bit and moves on. The first object found with a clear bit is evicted.

fig.caption.en: Eviction hand over eight objects. Objects with a set bit survive one pass of the hand.

burst.def.en: News traffic arrives in bursts: an article is requested thousands of times within minutes, then rarely again.

burst.k.def.en: SCB adds a burst bit that is set when an object is hit more than k=8 times within one sweep of the hand.

burst.rule.en: The hand clears the burst bit first and the reference bit on its next pass, so a burst buys exactly one extra pass.

lru.cost.en: LRU tracks recency exactly, but it moves an object on every hit, which costs a lock and a cache line on busy servers.

concl.en: Two bits per object recover most of LRU's hit rate on bursty traffic without updating metadata on every hit.

eval.trace.en: We replay a 24-hour trace with 41.3 million requests over 2.6 million objects, with a cache of 5% of the objects.
